title: An Asynchronous Object Detection Framework for TEM Data Analytics
content: Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) has become a de facto technique in materials science, functioning as a versatile tool for academic and industrial applications. Recent advancements in high-speed cameras and automated data acquisition now allow the generation of several hundred gigabytes to terabytes of data during a single user session. However, effectively storing, transferring, and processing such large amounts of data continues to present a significant challenge, hindering the goal of real-time feedback during experimental sessions. Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly in pattern recognition tasks, has revolutionized the field of object detection and tracking with remarkable speed and accuracy across applications like autonomous vehicles and video surveillance. Many TEM analysis tasks demand rapid and precise object identification and tracking. However, large-scale data streaming in TEM often encounters bottlenecks due to I/O constraints and CPU/GPU-bound operations, leading to high latency in information flow that hampers process efficiency.
